meta.title: TMU Table A Lower-Level Liberal Studies -- Engineering-Eligible Courses
meta.verificationMethodology: Every course record's courseCode, courseName, liberalStudiesLevel (LL), and engineeringEligible flag are verified against the official TMU Table A listing page itself (tableASourceUrl), which is a legitimate primary source for that data. Full narrative description, weekly contact hours, GPA weight, and requisite fields are only populated where they were individually confirmed against a specific TMU calendar course page in this project's research sessions -- see descriptionSourceUrl and descriptionSourceEdition per record. Records without those fields are marked verificationStatus: NEEDS_VERIFICATION and must not be treated as complete; the 'estimated' block (difficulty, workload flags, interest tags) is intentionally left empty for all records pending the interest-taxonomy milestone.
knownDataQualityNotes: BPM 474's course record title is 'Christian Music: Songs of Hope' in the official 2026-2027 course page, but it is cross-referenced as 'Gospel Music: Songs for the Spirit' in the 2026-2027 Media Elective Table II program page -- likely an updated working title not yet propagated to the course record itself. Flagged, not resolved.

ASL 201, LAT 200, MHK 201, MUS 101/201/220, and BPM 406/441 descriptions were confirmed via 2025-2026 (or earlier) calendar snapshots because a fresh 2026-2027 search/fetch did not surface the full narrative text; the description content itself has been stable across multiple editions checked, but this is noted as a caveat rather than presented as a fresh 2026-2027 confirmation.
ARB 201 and BPM 484 have confirmed requisite/restriction data but no confirmed narrative description -- explicitly left null rather than inferred from the title.

Phase 1 (course-data completion pass): 88 of 121 courses were researched against the official 2026-2027 TMU Undergraduate Calendar. CRB 100's antirequisite is officially listed as 'SYC 183' -- a subject-code prefix not otherwise present in this dataset or current TMU listings; recorded verbatim from the official course page as a data-quality note, not altered.

POH 105's programRestrictions could not be reliably confirmed in this pass: an initial web search suggested a restriction against Occupational Health and Safety program students, but a direct fetch of the official 2026-2027 course page did not show this text. Left as NEEDS_VERIFICATION for this field pending a second independent check -- do not treat as confirmed-none.
SOC 103's antirequisite list includes 'SOC 11 A/B', a legacy-format course code recorded verbatim from the official 2026-2027 page.

Phase 1 addendum: ASC 121 and ENG 112 (previously VERIFIED but sourced from an unconfirmed 2025-2026 page) were independently reconfirmed against the live 2026-2027 TMU calendar. All factual content matched (ENG 112's programRestrictions had a trivial Oxford-comma difference only, not a factual change). Provenance updated to 2026-2027 for both; no field values changed.

verified.description: Early modern Europe was torn by contradiction and conflict. Rediscovery of the ancients and reinterpretation of the Bible produced a new culture but split Christianity. courses.courseName: East Meets West: Asia in the World

verified.description: Where does East meet West? By exploring the role of Asia in globalization, Western colonialism in Asia, the world wars and the emergence of contemporary Asia, this course demonstrates how boundaries have been contested and (re)defined through military, political, commercial, cultural, and religious exchanges. It allows students to rethink common categories such as race, region, nation, culture, and civilization from an international perspective.

courses.courseName: Rise of Empires: History Through Film

verified.description: Can film provide valid insight into our past? How do we understand film as historical artifact? This course tries to answer these questions and many others by exploring films which deal with early European imperialism, that is, from the time of Columbus to the end of the First World War. The topics will be international in scope, drawing on aspects of Asian, African, and Latin American history, and examining both "blockbuster" and independent films.

verified.description: The French Revolution launched the modern age, in politics, society, the family, the arts, and war. The 19th century brought fresh revolutions: technology and industrialization transformed work and leisure, life and death; liberalism and revolutionary socialism challenged the old order; and science altered forever humanity's place in the universe. verified.description: African traditions have fed into and shaped many genres of popular music around the globe, including funk, soul, reggae, son, salsa, zouk, rap, house and grime. verified.description: What is considered popular culture is up for debate. This course examines different ideas about popular culture and how they inform our personal politics, consumption practices, and common-sense ideas about the world.
